report.tagline: India's biggest fashion shopping app, owned by Flipkart, now also delivering clothes in 30 minutes through M-Now.
report.simpleSummary: Myntra is an app for buying clothes, shoes, watches and beauty products from thousands of brands like Nike, H&M, Biba and Roadster. You can try clothes at home and send back what does not fit. In some cities, M-Now brings your order in 30 minutes. Myntra makes money by taking a cut from brands on every sale, charging for delivery, and selling ads to brands.

overview.whatItDoes: Myntra is a fashion marketplace. Brands and sellers list clothes, footwear, accessories and beauty products, and Myntra handles the app, delivery and returns. Flipkart bought it in 2014 and it runs as Flipkart's fashion arm.
howItWorks: Brands list styles on Myntra. Myntra takes a commission on each sale and charges for warehousing and delivery.
Buyers browse by brand, price, trend or occasion, and get recommendations based on what they viewed.
Orders are shipped from Myntra warehouses or seller locations. Most arrive in 2 to 5 days.
M-Now stocks popular styles in small city warehouses and delivers in about 30 minutes.
Buyers can return most items within the return window, and Myntra picks them up from home.
Big sales like End of Reason Sale (EORS) and Big Fashion Festival bring huge traffic bursts.
overview.valueProposition: Thousands of brands in one place, trend-led discovery, and easy returns, so you can buy clothes online without fear of getting the wrong size.

businessModel.summary: Myntra makes money in three main ways: a commission and service fee on each sale, delivery and logistics charges, and ads that brands buy. Its biggest costs are marketing, delivery and returns.

revenueStreams.detail: Commission and fees from brands on each sale. ₹2,657 crore in FY26.
Brands paying for visibility. ₹1,236 crore in FY26, up 35%.
Charges for warehousing, delivery and returns. ₹1,119 crore in FY26.
Platform fees, convenience fees and other services. ₹230 crore in FY26.

businessModel.pricing: Free to use. Products at brand prices with discounts. Buyers may pay a platform fee and a delivery fee below a minimum order value. Some returns carry a fee. Brands pay a commission that usually ranges from about 15% to 30% depending on category (estimate).
costDrivers: Marketing and promotions: ₹2,326 crore in FY26, about 40% of costs
Reverse logistics, which means picking up and checking returns
Staff and tech: ₹777 crore on employees
businessModel.unitEconomics: Take a ₹1,200 order. Myntra might earn about ₹250 to ₹300 from commission, fees and ads. Delivery costs about ₹60 to ₹80, and payment fees around ₹20. If the item is returned, which happens often in fashion, Myntra pays for the pickup and checking, about ₹60 to ₹80 more, and earns almost nothing. So one returned order can wipe out the profit of the next kept order. Add heavy marketing, and you see why Myntra is near breakeven and why cutting returns is its biggest lever.

howTheyGetUsers: Big sales like EORS and Big Fashion Festival, backed by TV and digital ads
Cross-promotion from Flipkart's large user base
whatBringsUsersBack: New styles every day and personalised feed
Myntra Insider points and early access
Easy returns that make the next order feel safe
growth.moat: Myntra has deep ties with thousands of fashion brands, years of data on what Indians buy and return by size and city, and a strong brand as the fashion destination. Matching this needs years of brand partnerships and large spending.

northStar.metric: Number of fashion orders kept (not returned) per month
northStar.why: A kept order means the buyer found something that fit and liked it. It captures discovery, fit and trust, and pushes the team to reduce returns rather than just push more orders.

pmLessons: In fashion, returns can decide whether you make money. Fixing fit is as important as getting the sale.
Speed is becoming a feature even in fashion. M-Now shows how a big player responds before startups grow.
Ads can become a big business when you own the place where buyers search.
Marketing can buy traffic, but only good fit and easy returns bring people back.

interviewQuestions.question: Myntra's returns are high. How would you reduce them without hurting sales?
interviewQuestions.hint: Break returns into reasons (size, look, quality, changed mind). Pick the biggest, propose size profiles and buyer photos, and set guardrails on conversion rate.

interviewQuestions.question: Is 30-minute fashion delivery worth it for Myntra?
interviewQuestions.hint: Define the user need (urgent events), look at costs (city stock, riders), compare with order value and repeat use, and suggest where it makes sense.

interviewQuestions.question: What should Myntra's north star metric be?
interviewQuestions.hint: Argue for kept orders, then build drivers: buyers, frequency, kept rate and selection.

interviewQuestions.question: How would you design Myntra's experience for a first-time buyer from a Tier-2 city?
interviewQuestions.hint: Look at trust, language, price and payment. Suggest a simple onboarding, local trends and cash on delivery, and measure first-order conversion.

interviewQuestions.question: Myntra's ad revenue is growing fast. How do you stop ads from making search worse?
interviewQuestions.hint: Talk about relevance, labelling, limits on ad slots, and guardrails like search to order rate.

assumptions: Monthly users of 70 to 80 million is an estimate. Myntra has not published a recent exact figure.
Commission range of 15% to 30% is an industry estimate.
Per-order costs in unit economics are rough estimates based on public cost lines, not company figures.
The fall in logistics revenue is assumed to come from an accounting change in how delivery fees are recorded.
